50: If you invest a dollar in India, you get part of India’s growth, but a good deal less than the growth of its economy (GDP) suggests. What you actually earn depends on company profits, the price you pay for shares (valuation), new shares that shrink your stake (dilution), how much a foreign investor is able to buy (investability), and the exchange rate when you bring the money home. India’s long-term case is strong, the price you pay matters a lot, and India has to be weighed against the other markets competing for the same money. The study answers its question about India by comparing India with other emerging markets.
52: The findings use data up to 31 July 2026. Nothing in the study is live data.
